rationale: This article examines architectural and urban design strategies for making generic infrastructures visible in a public plaza (the Square of General Vara del Rey) to foster civic engagement. It does not study household or community water or sanitation service access, legal or administrative mechanisms governing service delivery, or water/sanitation access outcomes (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both readings because the article is an architectural/urban design case study of a public square and generic infrastructural visibility, not household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: The aim of this article is to explore new ways of integrating technology, nature and infrastructures into urban public spaces.
This is done through a case study, the design of General Vara del Rey, which is offered here as a model to explore a novel urban political ecology
